criteria.text: For the selected AI scenarios, is the correct affected configuration item identifiable in the CMDB?
criteria.why: The impact workflow needs the affected CI identifier to determine where dependency tracing begins. Wrong or ambiguous CI records can produce an incorrect analysis.
criteria.evidence: Sample incident or change records with the affected CI, CI identifiers and a check for duplicate or obsolete entries.
criteria.improve: Correct the CI reference on selected records and resolve duplicate or obsolete CI entries.
criteria.learn: Whether an assessor can identify the intended configuration item reliably before AI analysis is enabled. A change or incident record can point to the CI, or the CI can be supplied directly.

criteria.text: For AI incident categorisation, are the affected configuration items associated with the correct services and service offerings?
criteria.why: Some incident categorisation experiences use service associations to identify which service or offering is affected. This criterion is not a universal requirement for CMDB impact analysis.
criteria.evidence: Samples of affected CIs and mapped service and service offering fields for the selected incident types.
criteria.improve: Correct the service associations used for incident categorisation.
criteria.learn: Whether service associations support the selected incident categorisation scenarios. It does not establish the quality of the dependency graph used by the impact analysis agent.

criteria.text: Does the CMDB contain accurate dependency relationships showing which other CIs and services depend on each affected CI?
criteria.why: The documented impact workflow traces upstream dependencies using CMDB relationships in cmdb_rel_ci. Missing or incorrectly directed relationships can hide impacted components and services.
criteria.evidence: Review direct relationship records in cmdb_rel_ci. Trace sample dependency paths from the affected CI and compare them with known impacts.
criteria.improve: Correct missing, inaccurate or reversed dependency relationships relevant to the selected scenarios.
criteria.learn: Whether AI can follow reliable dependency paths from the affected CI to components or services potentially impacted by the selected change or incident.

criteria.text: Are the CI records and dependency relationships needed for the selected impact scenarios accurate and sufficiently current?
criteria.why: AI reasons over the CMDB context it receives. Old or inaccurate CI data and relationships weaken the impact assessment.
criteria.evidence: Sample record checks against maintained sources, last update information and confirmation of relevant dependency accuracy.
criteria.improve: Update stale CI information and correct inaccurate dependency records.
criteria.learn: Whether the selected dependency data accurately represents the environment being assessed.

criteria.text: Is there an accountable owner and a correction process for defects in the relevant CI and dependency data?
criteria.why: This is an independent governance recommendation. ServiceNow does not list the existence of a named correction owner as an invocation prerequisite, but persistent defects weaken repeated AI assessments.
criteria.evidence: Named data owners, sample data quality remediation records and a repeatable correction process.
criteria.improve: Identify accountable data owners and establish a defect correction procedure.
criteria.learn: Whether discovered CMDB defects have a route to remediation, rather than continuing to affect future AI analyses.

criteria.text: In a configured environment, can an authorised user invoke impact analysis and read the required CMDB and incident or change information?
criteria.why: The documented workflow requires appropriate access, including the itil role for reading relevant records and invoking impact analysis. Access needs to be tested after configuration.
criteria.evidence: Positive and negative access tests with appropriate user roles, the relevant incident or change records and impact analysis invocation.
criteria.improve: Confirm the required roles and permissions, then retest the configured impact workflow.
criteria.learn: Whether the chosen user and configured experience can carry out the documented operation using authorised permissions.

criteria.text: For each selected impact scenario, is there a clear description of the proposed change or incident for AI to assess?
criteria.why: The documented impact workflow uses a change or incident description alongside the affected CI. Vague descriptions reduce the quality of AI reasoning about likely impact.
criteria.learn: Whether enough information about the planned change or incident is available for the AI to reason about the scope and possible consequences.
criteria.evidence: Representative incident or change descriptions, including the action, affected CI, purpose and operational context. A direct invocation can supply a CI identifier and description.
criteria.improve: Improve change or incident descriptions so the proposed action, affected CI and operational context are clear.

criteria.text: Do approved articles cover the actual questions and incident categories selected for this AI capability?
criteria.why: Content outside the selected demand patterns does not support useful answers or resolutions.
criteria.evidence: Top incident categories and queries mapped to relevant published articles.
criteria.improve: Prioritise coverage of the common scoped incidents and questions.
criteria.learn: Whether approved knowledge covers the real questions and incident categories within the chosen AI scope. Missing coverage becomes a priority for knowledge preparation.

criteria.text: For selected incident types, are the instructions complete, ordered and usable by the intended audience?
criteria.why: Autonomous investigation requires repeatable procedures, not merely topic descriptions.
criteria.evidence: Subject matter review and walkthrough of sample diagnosis and resolution steps.
criteria.improve: Rewrite procedures with prerequisites, diagnostic steps and expected results.
criteria.learn: Whether the selected incident procedures contain enough ordered detail for an AI assistant or specialist to follow safely and consistently.

criteria.text: Are operational decisions, exceptions, unsafe conditions and escalation triggers documented rather than known only to experienced staff?
criteria.why: The tacit tax arises when the knowledge AI needs remains informal and inaccessible.
criteria.evidence: Analyst interviews, exception tables, policy conditions and escalation walkthroughs.
criteria.improve: Capture undocumented decision rules, exceptions and escalation boundaries.
criteria.learn: Whether undocumented analyst judgement, exceptions and escalation rules would create gaps when work is delegated to AI.

criteria.text: Have relevant articles been validated for accuracy and contradictions against current operational practice?
criteria.why: Conflicting or incorrect instructions can make grounded answers unreliable.
criteria.evidence: Article owner sign off and sampled comparison with real working practices.
criteria.improve: Resolve contradictory guidance and validate material instructions with service owners.
criteria.learn: Whether the knowledge used for generated answers and resolution steps is accurate and free from conflicting instructions.

criteria.text: Are the relevant articles clearly structured, described by metadata and maintained through a review process?
criteria.why: Well structured, current content improves retrievability and interpretation.
criteria.evidence: Article templates, metadata completeness, review dates and stale content reports.
criteria.improve: Apply consistent templates and establish scheduled maintenance.
criteria.learn: Whether relevant articles are organised and maintained so that the intended AI experience can interpret and retrieve them reliably.

criteria.text: Can the selected AI experience retrieve the relevant published articles through its configured search sources and profiles?
criteria.why: A correct article offers no value if the AI experience cannot find it.
criteria.evidence: Index status, source and search profile configuration, query test results.
criteria.improve: Correct indexing and search profile configuration, then test representative queries.
criteria.learn: Whether the AI Search configuration actually retrieves suitable published articles for representative questions.

criteria.text: Do knowledge retrieval and generated responses respect the intended user and agent access restrictions?
criteria.why: Restricted articles must not appear in responses to unauthorised users.
criteria.evidence: Positive and negative access tests with appropriate identities and content classes.
criteria.improve: Fix access controls and retest restricted retrieval before any pilot.
criteria.learn: Whether knowledge retrieval and generated responses protect restricted information for the relevant user and agent identities.

criteria.text: Are active catalogue items available for the request types the selected AI experience must recognise or fulfil?
criteria.why: AI needs a valid target for intended requests and redirection.
criteria.evidence: Request demand mapped to active items and allowed requester audiences.
criteria.improve: Prioritise missing items for common request intents.
criteria.learn: Whether valid catalogue destinations exist for the requests the AI experience is expected to recognise or fulfil.

criteria.text: Are catalogue item names, descriptions and guidance clear enough for AI to distinguish similar requests?
criteria.why: Ambiguous item descriptions increase incorrect request selection.
criteria.evidence: Item metadata review and sample utterance matching checks.
criteria.improve: Clarify labels, descriptions, eligibility and alternative request paths.
criteria.learn: Whether the intended AI experience can distinguish similar catalogue items using their descriptions and eligibility information.

criteria.text: Do the items selected for conversational ordering meet the requirements of the chosen Catalog Agent experience?
criteria.why: Unsupported item configurations fall back to a form or prevent a full conversation.
criteria.evidence: Conversational coverage report and checks for supported variables and scripting.
criteria.improve: Review item eligibility for the specific mechanism and keep safe form fallback.
criteria.learn: Whether selected items can be handled by the specific conversational catalogue capability, rather than unexpectedly falling back to forms.

criteria.text: Can the conversation collect and correctly validate the mandatory information needed to submit those requests?
criteria.why: Incomplete or incorrectly mapped variables produce failed or unsuitable requests.
criteria.evidence: Variable mapping tests, mandatory field scenarios and conditional input examples.
criteria.improve: Simplify variables or implement supported validation and dialogue flows.
criteria.learn: Whether the conversational flow can collect complete, valid request data before submission.

criteria.text: Are user eligibility, entitlements and approval rules enforced by the underlying ServiceNow workflow?
criteria.why: An AI recommendation must not bypass access and approval controls.
criteria.evidence: Request impersonation cases, positive and negative authorisation tests, approval history.
criteria.improve: Enforce user criteria and approvals at platform level, then retest.
criteria.learn: Whether the platform enforces requester eligibility and approval policies even when the request begins in an AI conversation.

criteria.text: Do AI initiated submissions create the correct request records and enter a working fulfilment process?
criteria.why: Successful conversational intake is insufficient without controlled downstream execution.
criteria.evidence: Test order record, fulfilment owner, approval status and tracking history.
criteria.improve: Fix fulfilment integration and verify record creation and tracking.
criteria.learn: Whether an AI initiated request produces the correct records and can be tracked through real fulfilment.

criteria.text: When a request is unclear or unsupported, does the experience provide safe clarification, form fallback or human escalation?
criteria.why: The system must handle exceptions without inventing or forcing unsafe requests.
criteria.evidence: Ambiguous, cancelled and unsupported request tests and fallback results.
criteria.improve: Document and test the clarification and fallback routes.
criteria.learn: Whether ambiguous or unsupported requests have a safe way to clarify, redirect or reach a human rather than producing an unsuitable request.

capabilities.name: L1 IT Service Desk AI Specialist
capabilities.summary: Resolve selected L1 incidents with procedural knowledge, historical context and supported catalogue or CI activities where those scenarios apply.

optional.label: Include incident redirection or access requests using catalogue items
Include incident investigation that uses CI and service context

capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: Procedural articles, documented exceptions and authorised search support investigation and resolution.

Catalogue.reason: Catalogue information supports identifying incidents that are actually requests, suggesting an appropriate item and eligible request scenarios. It is not necessary for every incident.

CMDB.reason: CI identity and service context matter when the selected L1 workflow classifies CIs or investigates a configuration related issue. Full dependency topology is not a universal prerequisite.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

capabilities.name: AI Search and Otto knowledge answers
capabilities.summary: Grounded knowledge responses to approved user questions.
capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: Approved published articles, correct indexing and authorised retrieval support grounded answers.

Catalogue.reason: The selected profile tests knowledge answers, not conversational item selection or ordering.

CMDB.reason: No CMDB activity is selected in this knowledge answer profile.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

capabilities.name: ITSM AI incident triage and categorisation
capabilities.summary: Classification of relevant configuration items, services and offerings.
capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: The selected triage profile does not assess resolution knowledge.

Catalogue.reason: The documented workflow classifies services and service offerings, not request catalogue items.

CMDB.reason: The workflow assigns relevant CIs, services and service offerings when classifying incidents.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

capabilities.name: ITSM AI investigation workflow
capabilities.summary: Investigate incidents using relevant knowledge and available record context.

optional.label: Include investigation based on CI and service context
Include request redirection with clarification or human fallback

capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: The documented resolution investigation uses relevant knowledge articles and similar incidents.

Catalogue.reason: The documented investigation workflow searches for and recommends related catalogue items; this is distinct from submitting an order.

CMDB.reason: CI context is relevant when the chosen investigation also uses related configuration records or the Incident Assist experience.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

capabilities.name: Now Assist CMDB impact analysis
capabilities.summary: Assess whether the correct affected CI, change or incident context and CMDB dependency paths can support an AI impact assessment.
capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: The documented impact calculation does not require a knowledge article corpus.

Catalogue.reason: Catalogue item eligibility is not an input to the documented dependency topology traversal.

CMDB.reason: The impact workflow needs an affected CI, a meaningful change or incident description and upstream dependency relationships.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

capabilities.name: Catalog Agent conversational requests
capabilities.summary: Find suitable items, collect required information and submit authorised requests.
capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: Knowledge may enhance an extended journey but is not a core input to this catalogue ordering profile.

Catalogue.reason: The Catalog Agent needs eligible items, variable definitions, requester rules and functioning fulfilment.

CMDB.reason: CMDB relationships are not a general prerequisite for conversational catalogue ordering.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

capabilities.name: Otto conversational request journey
capabilities.summary: Help a user find and complete an eligible catalogue request.

optional.label: Also include knowledge answers during the request journey

capabilities.preparationNote: The preparation assessment does not prove that this capability is configured, permitted or capable of reliable execution.

Knowledge.reason: A combined conversational journey may answer knowledge questions before or during a request.

Catalogue.reason: This selected Otto journey is for conversational service requests and depends on eligible catalogue items.

CMDB.reason: The selected conversational request journey does not assess CI impact analysis.

capabilities.otherRequirements: Additional technical and operational requirements such as incident history, AI entitlements, assignment routing, access policy and controlled testing are outside this three foundation assessment.

responseRubric.yes: The criterion is satisfied in the selected scope. Supporting evidence should be available.
responseRubric.partial: The condition is present in some scenarios, but gaps remain.
responseRubric.no: The criterion is not satisfied in the selected scope.
responseRubric.unknown: Not enough information has been gathered to make a claim.
responseRubric.na: Excluded by the assessor with a written scope justification. This does not confirm the requirement is irrelevant.

evidenceRubric.reviewed: Assessor reports inspecting supporting records or documents.
evidenceRubric.tested: Assessor reports running representative checks. The application does not independently verify these claims.
